summary.text: Tim Taylor is a Republican member of the Missouri House of Representatives, District 48, who assumed office on January 6, 2021 and is seeking re-election in the November 3, 2026 general election.
Taylor served in the U.S. Air Force and worked as a firefighter and captain with the Columbia Fire Department.

paragraphs.text: Tim Taylor was born in Mexico, Missouri, and served in the U.S. Air Force from 1987 to 1991.

His career experience includes working as a firefighter and captain with the Columbia Fire Department, as an emergency medical technician, as a fire service instructor, and as a non-commissioned officer with the U.S. Air Force Security Police Academy.

Taylor has been affiliated with the Thoma-Tuttle Post 52 of the American Legion, the National Rifle Association as an instructor, the Missouri Farm Bureau and the Cooper County Historical Society, among other organizations.
In the Missouri House, Taylor was assigned to the Budget Committee and the Conservation and Natural Resources Committee for 2025-2026.
He served as vice chair of the Conservation and Natural Resources Committee in 2023-2024.
